An RS485 transceiver contains a driver and a receiver.

When the DE (Driver Enable) signal is 1, the driver is enabled; when DE is 0, the driver is disabled.
The UART receiver converts differential signals to single-ended signals via an external receiver.
RE is the enable control signal for the receiver.
When RE is 0, the receiver is enabled; when RE is 1, the receiver is disabled.
If RE is configured as 0, the UART controller is allowed to snoop data on the bus, including the data sent by itself.
DE can be controlled by either software or hardware.
To reduce the cost of software, DE is controlled by hardware in our design.
